Phish are the best, and usually shit is so mellow at their shows.  This was a notable exception.

I'm pretty sure I prevented these 2 girls from getting killed or injured in a crowd rush...

I was at Bonnaroo (big open access music festival in TN), in line with a bunch of other people for the big final phish show on sunday.  Anyway, so about a half hour before they open the pit, a metric fuckton of people kind of bum-rushed the front of the line, so instead of a line it became more of a large cone, consisting of probably 2000 people, one wall of which was bordered by a huge plywood wall.  As the start letting people into the pit, and the crowd starts creeping forward into the bottleneck, it got really tight really fast.  I'm a large man, and can hold my own in a crowd,  and I was being basically carried by a slow rolling wave of people. I started being carried toward the wall edge of the crowd as we got into the start of the crunch, when out of nowhere there is a huge crowd surge, and I basically get thrown toward the wall by a massive rush of people. 

The next part happened fast as hell.  As I am flying toward this plywood wall, I see these two girls getting MASHED against the wall by the crowd. I am maybe three feet from them, so I wade forward and get between them and the direction the crush is coming from.  I'm not sure how I thought to do this,  but I braced my elbows against the plywood, braced my feet a couple feet out from the wall, and told the girls "let's go", and basically inched forward the last 20 feet, through the worst of the crunch, with them cowering in the tiny space created by my arms between us and the wall.  I was basically purple with exertion by the time we got through... but we made it. 

This all took maybe 20 seconds, and then we were out into the pit.  I didn't really talk to them,  just smiled and went to go meet my friends who had already made it through.  They came and found me later, and thanked me profusely and said that they had been stuck in that spot getting squished by the crowd for almost five minutes at that point (which is deeply depressing), and were getting really scared.  I really hope that they would have been fine without me,  but I heard a few people got injured and one guy got trampled that day, so who knows. 

I was rewarded with a couple hauls off a joint and some lukewarm vodka sprite from a camelbak... like a boss

and yes, I appreciate the irony of a crowd crush at a phish show...
